title: Protection & Other-Trade Damage
short_answer: Protect what we finished. Photograph what others damage before we touch it. The moment we repair undocumented damage, it becomes ours.
summary: Corner guards, floor protection, and covering finished walls are not courtesy — they are how we keep punch from eating the margin.
plain_words: Corner guards, floor protection, and covering finished walls are not courtesy — they are how we keep punch from eating the margin. If another trade blows out a corner, photo first, then call. Fixing it as a favor is unpaid drywall.
when_to_use: Before leaving an area where other trades still work
When you find damage that another trade likely caused
Before repairing anything that might become a billable CO
prerequisites: Lead or office path for authorization on other-trade damage

tools.name: Corner guards / ram board / floor protection

materials.name: Ram board, masonite, or GC-approved floor protection
Plastic or paper for finished walls

steps.title: Before we leave an area
steps.body: Protect outside corners and finished surfaces that other trades will still work past.

steps.title: Floor / path protection
steps.body: Where mud, paint, or board traffic will ruin finished floors — coordinate with GC rules.

steps.title: Other-trade damage
steps.body: Wide + close photo, location, date, who was in the area if known — then lead/office.

steps.title: Do not repair yet
steps.body: Do not repair until authorization path is clear (T&M / CO / GC direction in writing). See Spotting a Change Order.

steps.title: Our own rework
steps.body: Our own damage / our own rework stays ours — claiming it as a CO spends credibility.

warnings.title: Photo before touch
warnings.body: The moment we repair undocumented other-trade damage, it becomes ours. Photo first, call second, repair only with authorization.

quality_checks.prompt: Outside corners and finished surfaces protected before other trades pass through
Other-trade damage photographed before any repair
Repair authorization clear before work starts on billable damage

common_mistakes.title: Friendly repair
common_mistakes.wrong: Fix the electrician's blowout so the room looks good
common_mistakes.right: Photo, call lead/office, wait for CO or T&M path

common_mistakes.title: Claiming our rework
common_mistakes.wrong: Submit a CO for damage we caused
common_mistakes.right: Own our rework; save CO credibility for real extras
common_mistakes.why: Bad COs poison the well for legitimate ones
